name: Andy Beshear
role: Governor of Kentucky (since 2019); Kentucky Attorney General (2016-2019)
summary: Democratic governor of a Republican-leaning state who frames his politics as pragmatic and results-focused ('not right, not left, but forward'). His record shows support for unions, public schools, Medicaid expansion and abortion and LGBTQ rights (through vetoes later overridden), with pro-business, pro-gun-rights and law-enforcement-funding elements. He supports constitutional changes such as term limits for Congress and the Supreme Court and direct election of the president.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Calls health care a basic human right and fully funds Medicaid expansion, but says the private sector often provides care and favors government drug-price negotiation and transparency over a government-provided system; stays open to talks on Medicare for All.

unions-good.rationale: In his 2026 address he thanked unions, said being pro-union creates jobs and opportunity, and said unions have fought for the American Dream; he says he vetoed every anti-union bill.

cut-welfare.rationale: Vetoed HB 7 (2022) over new barriers to SNAP and Medicaid, and in 2026 proposed $50 million for food banks and full Medicaid funding against federal SNAP and Medicaid cuts.

limit-guns.rationale: Backs a red flag law and vetoed concealed carry for under-21s, but says he supports the Second Amendment and everyone's ability to defend their family.

empower-police-military.rationale: His budgets raised State Police pay, added troopers and funded local police training; no statement on added authority.

rehabilitation.rationale: Proposed a reentry campus and prison vocational programs, cites record-low recidivism, and says his faith calls for second chances.

abortion-legal.rationale: Vetoed HB 3 (no rape or incest exceptions) and HB 90 (life-saving care), and says he has vetoed every anti-choice bill; no stated gestational standard.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Vetoing HB 4, said hundreds of years of inequality have not been overcome and that diversity programs help include communities of color.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Said employers need more immigration and that comprehensive reform is needed.

open-borders.rationale: Said border security is national security and that immigration laws must be enforced.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Welcomed a $1.5 billion General Matter investment to bring modern nuclear power to Paducah; no stated position on nuclear power generally.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Says tariffs are a tax on Americans and that he, both U.S. senators and business are against them; says they raise costs and cause layoffs.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Calls himself a pragmatist focused on results, saying success is not red or blue, left or right.

school-vouchers.rationale: Vetoed HB 563 (2021), which routed public money through account-granting organizations to private schools, as harming public schools and unconstitutional; calls himself a 100% pro-public-education governor.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Vetoes and orders rest on all children being children of God and discrimination against LGBTQ+ Kentuckians being unacceptable; vetoed HB 4 saying diversity is a strength.

separated-powers.rationale: His SB 1 (2021) veto argues the Constitution's separation of powers and checks bar the legislature from limiting executive emergency power.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Said it is time for direct election of the president and vice president, abolishing the Electoral College.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Vetoed HB 18 (2024) because it let landlords refuse housing to people using federal assistance, and signed an order opposing discrimination.

corporate-influence.rationale: Called for a constitutional amendment overturning Citizens United.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Vetoed SB 150 and SB 83, which restricted transgender youth care, naming and sports; defended gender-affirming care and KHSAA transgender participation policy.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Says Kentucky moves 'not right, not left, but forward' and that success is not left or right, while remaining a Democrat.

term-limits.rationale: Called for a constitutional amendment creating term limits for Congress and the Supreme Court.

voter-id.rationale: Vetoed SB 2 (2020) requiring photo ID to vote, saying it creates an obstacle to voting and addresses a problem that does not exist.

indirect-election.rationale: Supports direct election of the president and vice president rather than by an electoral college.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: In the HB 4 veto he called acting as if racism and discrimination no longer exist disingenuous.

notes: Most answers come from his veto messages and addresses. Many statements are null because he has not spoken to them or only a nearby issue is documented (death penalty, recreational drugs, same-sex marriage, minimum wage, climate and foreign policy have no cited primary source in this audit). He has said he supports the death penalty for some crimes, but only a news report of that was not opened, so it is left null. As of 2026 he is a prospective 2028 presidential candidate and chair of the Democratic Governors Association.
